title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-04-29
content:
Weekly update / standup log - serving runtime (kernel work, KV cache, batching)

Date: 2026-04-29
Owner: Ava Martinez
Attendees: Riley, Priya, Liam, Sofia, Jordan, Ava
Duration: 45m

OVERVIEW:
- Focus this week: finalize attention-kernel rewrite, stabilize sharded KV cache under high concurrency, and land dynamic batching changes for mixed-latency workloads.
- Quick status: kernel rewrite in final review; KV cache still flapping for multi-tenant bursts; batching gives solid throughput uplift but needs improved backpressure handling.

KERNEL WORK:
- PR #1247: attention-kernel rewrite (vectorized/sliding-window approach). In review, addressed most comments from Marco/Devon.
  - Local perf: +18% throughput for long-context (8k-132k) tests; p50 tokens down ~12ms on A100-80GB emulation.
  - Memory: more contiguous KV layout reduces scatter, observed small reduction in CUDA memcopies.
  - TODO: add additional microbenchmarks for short-context (<=512) to ensure no regressions; Priya to run test suite and report by Tue 05/05.
- Follow-ups: validate kernel on pinned-quantized builds (q4_0). Some kernels hit fp16 corner-case; Jordan opened bug (JIRA-RT-904).

KV CACHE:
- Sharded KV cache: aim is reduce lock contention by per-shard LRU. Current behaviour: under high-concurrency bursts (50k reqs/min across tenants) we see ~1.4% token duplication due to stale prefix hits + occasional eviction storms.
  - Investigation: eviction storm correlated with mixed-length sequences from same connection; small prefixes evict hot entries.
  - Mitigation implemented: temporary conservative reservation policy for hot keys (protect top-5% by access frequency). Reduced duplication from 1.4% -> 0.3% in stress run.
- Consistency: race in async writeback causing occasional incorrect prefix IDs in telemetry. Repro steps + stack trace captured; fix in progress (Liam).
- Metrics observed: cache hit rate improved from 62% -> 69% with prefix-aware hotlist on internal workloads; token cost reduction ~12% on the eval set.
- TODOs:
  - Add unit tests for eviction ordering across shards (Liam, due 05/06).
  - Run end-to-end regression with real CS workload (Sofia to coordinate with CS sandbox).

BATCHING:
- Dynamic batching v2 rolled to canary yesterday. Key changes: adaptive bucket sizing based on recent sequence-length histogram + early-release when latency SLO at risk.
  - Canary results: throughput +9% on average, p95 latency improved by ~60ms for tail-heavy workloads.
  - Issue: under mixed workload with frequent small requests, we see occasional queueing spikes (p99 latency spikes); root cause likely our backpressure timeout heuristics.
- Proposed tweak: tighten max queue time from 50ms -> 30ms for burst-prone routes and enable immediate dispatch for requests flagged as latency-sensitive. Riley to prototype config gate by 05/04.
- Integration: updated batching metrics in console (route-level batch size histogram) shipped; need more retention on per-tenant breakdown for next sprint.

OPERATIONAL/OBSERVABILITY:
- Added tracing hooks to correlate KV-cache evictions with batching events; initial traces show eviction often follows a big batch from same worker.
- Cost telemetry: token/unit cost down ~7% in internal perf tests due to cache + batching improvements. Need to validate on longer runs.

BLOCKERS & RISKS:
- Kernel rewrite: fp16 corner-case with quantized variants — blocks rolling to dedicated pools. Blocking bug JIRA-RT-904.
- KV cache consistency bug (async writeback) causing rare bad telemetry and occasionally wrong retrievals for prefetched prefixes. High priority.
- Batching backpressure corner-cases under mixed traffic can cause p99 spikes — risk to SLO for some customers.

ACTION ITEMS (owners & ETA):
- Priya: run short-context microbenchmarks for new attention kernel; report regressions by 2026-05-05.
- Jordan: triage fp16 corner-case and prepare minimal repro + failing test; ETA 2026-05-03.
- Liam: implement unit tests for sharded eviction ordering and a fix for async writeback; ETA 2026-05-06.
- Sofia: schedule CS sandbox run and coordinate real-workload regression (end-to-end); ETA 2026-05-08.
- Riley: prototype tightened backpressure config and immediate-dispatch flag; demo on next sync (2026-05-04).
- Ava: prepare rollout plan for kernel v2 if all green (include canary gates, metrics to monitor, rollback plan).

DECISIONS MADE:
- Hold rollouts of kernel v2 to dedicated pools until fp16 repro fixed. Host canary remains ok for now.
- Enable prefix hotlist protection in KV cache as default for canary; we'll measure long-run stability before promoting to prod.

NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- How aggressive should hotlist protection be across tenants to avoid cross-tenant cache unfairness? (defer to arch review)
- Should latency-sensitive requests be flagged at API layer (application routing) or detected heuristically in runtime? Both approaches have tradeoffs.

NEXT WEEK PLAN (high level):
- Finish kernel kernelize PR review + short-context perf validation.
- Kill async writeback race and fortify eviction tests.
- Iterate batching backpressure config and run broader canary.
- Prepare detailed rollout checklist for kernel v2 (monitoring, telemetry, quick rollback).

MEETING NOTES / STANDUP LOGS (short):
- Mon: kernel PR feedback loop; KV eviction debug started.
- Tue: discovered fp16 quantization edge case; opened JIRA.
- Wed: initial canary run for batching v2; saw p99 spikes; started backpressure review.
- Thu: implemented hotlist protection; retested KV behaviour under burst.
- Fri: sync + writeup (this doc).

ADDITIONAL LINKS:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1247
- Kernel perf dashboards: confluence.redwood/serving-runtime/kernel-optimizations
- KV cache design notes: confluence.redwood/serving-runtime/kv-cache-design

TL;DR: good throughput gains from kernel + batching; KV cache stability still needs fixes. Prioritize async writeback fix and fp16 repro so kernel v2 can be promoted to broader pools.
